children.value: Vite

is the adapter for Vite 8 and Rolldown. It owns a compiler session,
compiles the modules that carry styles, serves the stylesheet in development and
writes it in a build.

children.value: In development

the plugin serves the live stylesheet and pushes updates
over Vite's hot channel, so a style change restyles the page without a reload.
A page that is still loading its modules on a cold start cannot take an
update yet; when the stylesheet runs, it tells the server which one it holds,
and the server sends a newer one. With

Vite delivers no
update, so the server tells the page the stylesheet changed and the stylesheet
fetches itself again (

Vitest
Vitest runs on Vite, so the plugin in your

compiles the modules
your tests import, to the class names the app ships. In browser mode, import the
stylesheet in a setup file, as your app's entry does:

properties.html: import { playwright } from "@vitest/browser-playwright" export default defineConfig({ plugins: [kirana(), react()], test: { setupFiles: ["./test/setup.ts"], browser: { enabled: true, provider: playwright(), instances: [{ browser: "chromium" }], }, }, })
properties.title: vite.config.ts

children.value:
Browser mode turns Vite's hot updates off, so a component a test imports
compiles after the page loaded the stylesheet, and no hot update can bring its
rules. The plugin tells the page the stylesheet changed, and the stylesheet
fetches itself again, a moment after the component's module compiled. Read a
style with an assertion that retries rather than right after mounting:

properties.html: import { expect, test } from "vitest" import { page } from "vitest/browser" test("the row wraps its items", async () => { const { mountRow } = await import("./row") mountRow(document.body) await expect.element(page.getByRole("list")).toHaveStyle({ flexWrap: "wrap" }) })
properties.title: row.test.ts

children.value:
The page's stylesheet is replaced only when its text changed, so an update that
adds nothing does not restyle the page and cut a running transition short.
A stylesheet of your own
Kirana's stylesheet keeps

as written. A stylesheet you write goes
through Vite's CSS minifier instead, and Vite's default

predates
that function, so the minifier rewrites it into switches on two custom properties
that nothing sets: colours that work in development vanish in production. Set the
target to Kirana's floor, Chrome 123, Safari 17.5, Firefox 120, the first browsers with it:

properties.html: export default defineConfig({ build: { cssTarget: ["chrome123", "safari17.5", "firefox120"] }, })
properties.title: vite.config.ts

children.value: Diagnostics in the terminal

Errors fail the build; warnings print with their file, line and help text. Info
diagnostics are quiet unless you pass

, which is useful when you
want to see every runtime bridge in an application.
Rolldown

Vite 8 is Rolldown-backed, and the plugin uses Rolldown's filters, so a
Rolldown-only setup works the same way.
